task/assembly.short_description: Putting parts together — insertions, fastening, connectors, clips — where the robot has to feel what it is doing rather than repeat a position.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Screwdriving and press-fit cells run in production at scale in electronics and automotive, so this is genuinely commercial — but every one of those cells was engineered for its part set, and nothing transfers. The category has revenue without leverage: each new part is a fresh integration project, and the flexible-assembly demonstrations that would change that are still demonstrations. Early commercial until a cell absorbs a new part without an engineer.
advance_criteria: Assembly cells requalified for a new product without re-tuning insertion strategies
Learned manipulation policies handling connectors and cables at production yield
Integrators quoting assembly cells at fixed price rather than as engineering time
regress_criteria: Continued growth of manual assembly in low-cost regions removing the pressure to automate at all

incumbent_process.text: Manual assembly at a bench or a moving line, with jigs, torque drivers and a trained operator absorbing every part variation without anyone writing it down.

assessment.author: editorial

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Every part in the stack is slightly wrong, and a position-controlled arm resolves the disagreement by breaking something. Contact force is the only signal that distinguishes seating from jamming.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by tolerances tight enough for blind insertion, which nobody pays for.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Cables, harnesses, clips and gaskets change shape while being held, which breaks the rigid-body assumption underneath most robot software. This is the single largest reason final assembly is still manual.
advance_criteria: Would be satisfied by production cells routing and seating wiring harnesses at line rate.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: An assembly cell that stops on every misfeed needs an attendant, and an attended cell has not removed the labour it was bought to remove.
advance_criteria: Would be satisfied by cells clearing their own faults across a shift.

task/cnc-machine-tending.short_description: Loading blanks into a machine tool and unloading finished parts, shift after shift, so the spindle keeps cutting.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: This is the reference case for industrial robotics. Cobot and caged tending cells are sold as configured products by every arm vendor, integrators quote them from a site photo, and the payback is a spreadsheet, not a pilot. Penetration is still low in job shops, but that gap is capital discipline and part variety, not an unsolved capability — which is exactly what separates a mature task from a scaling one.
advance_criteria: Already at the top of the scale; watch tending attach rates on new machine tool sales
Machine builders shipping robot-ready doors and interlocks as standard
regress_criteria: A safety-standard change that forces fencing back onto collaborative cells and destroys the small-shop economics

assessment.rationale: Collaborative picking AMRs run at thousands of sites, Locus alone reports billions of picks, and the model is sold as RaaS with predictable unit economics. It stops short of mature because the human picker is still in the loop and the next step, autonomous each-picking, is a different task.
advance_criteria: Default choice in new fulfilment-centre designs across regions
Multi-vendor price competition at commodity margins
Integration with autonomous picking arms in production sites

evidence_considered.sentence: Locus Robotics targets task Each-picking assistance
Locus fleets at 3PL sites serves task Each-picking assistance

incumbent_process.text: Pickers walking with carts and paper or RF pick lists.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Walking time is the majority of a manual picker's shift, which is the productivity gap the robots close.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: 3PLs buy for seasonal flexibility and roll out across sites.
advance_criteria: Stable.

market/energy.short_description: Generation and transmission assets: wind, solar, oil and gas, nuclear. Inspection and maintenance at height and in hazardous areas.

architecture_note.text: Figure 03 is presented as hardware designed around Helix, Figure's vision-language-action model, with the sensor suite and hands specified for that policy rather than for teleoperation.

market/healthcare.short_description: Surgical, hospital logistics, rehabilitation and lab automation.

task/in-process-inspection.short_description: Checking parts for dimensional and cosmetic defects on the line, rather than pulling samples to a quality lab afterwards.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Fixed machine vision has been production-standard for decades and learned defect detection is now shipping in real plants, not just pilots — which puts this well past early commercial. It is not mature because the two halves have not merged: the fixed station is validated but blind to new parts, and the learned model that handles variety still struggles to get through a quality department's sign-off. Scaling, with the sign-off problem as the gate.
advance_criteria: Learned defect models accepted as the system of record in customer quality systems
Inspection requalified for a new part without re-engineering the optics
Arm-mounted inspection matching fixed-station cycle times on production lines
regress_criteria: A quality escape traced to a learned model that pushes buyers back to rule-based vision

evidence_considered.sentence: Fixed machine vision station maturity MATURE

incumbent_process.text: An operator eyeballing parts against a boundary sample, plus a periodic trip to a CMM or gauge lab for dimensional checks on a sample.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Sampling means defects are found batches late, and human visual inspection degrades measurably across a shift — the two facts that fund every inspection automation project.
advance_criteria: Stable.

approaches.short_description: A camera on an arm walking a part through inspection poses, replacing a fixed multi-camera station with one moving eye.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Vendors ship arm-mounted inspection as a packaged cell and cobots now arrive with the camera built in, but most plants still buy a fixed vision station because it is faster and easier to validate. The moving camera earns its place only where part variety defeats fixed optics, which is a real but narrow slice today.
advance_criteria: Inspection cells requalified for a new part without re-engineering the optics
Learned defect models accepted in customer quality systems, not just as a pre-filter
Cycle times competitive with fixed multi-camera stations
regress_criteria: Cheaper high-resolution fixed stations removing the reason to move the camera

approaches.short_description: Cameras and lights bolted around a conveyor, inspecting every part in the same pose at line rate.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Fixed vision is a decades-old, thoroughly validated category with an entrenched vendor set and quality departments that already know how to sign it off. It is the incumbent any robotic inspection approach must beat, and on repeat parts it usually wins.
advance_criteria: Already at the top of the scale
regress_criteria: Part variety rising fast enough that fixed optics stop being requalifiable

technical_requirements.text: Defect definition that survives contact with production

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Plants routinely cannot state what counts as a defect in terms a system can measure, and inspectors disagree with each other. The labelling problem, not the vision problem, is what stalls these projects.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by anomaly detection that learns from good parts alone.

technical_requirements.text: Inspection inside the line's cycle time

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: An inspection that takes longer than the machine cycle becomes the bottleneck and gets switched off in the first busy week.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed where inspection runs off-line on a parallel station.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Machined, coated and reflective surfaces defeat naive imaging; the lighting design is usually a larger share of the engineering than the algorithm.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by imaging robust to specular surfaces without bespoke lighting.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Documented per-part inspection is contractually required in these supply chains, which converts inspection from a cost into an obligation.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Regulated traceability makes per-part inspection records valuable in themselves, independent of the labour saved.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: High volumes and small features make automated optical inspection standard practice rather than an upgrade.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: A learned inspection model has to be proven against the existing method to a quality department that carries the liability. That process is measured in months and is rarely in the vendor's project plan, which is why so many inspection pilots never turn into production systems.
advance_criteria: Statistically validated model performance accepted in place of a manual reference check
Regulated customers approving learned inspection in their quality systems

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Over-rejection scraps good parts and destroys the business case faster than missed defects do, because it is immediately visible on the yield report. Tuning the threshold is a commercial negotiation dressed up as a technical setting.
advance_criteria: False reject rates published and held below the manual baseline in production

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: A good plant makes very few defects, so the training set for the thing you care about is nearly empty. Vendors either manufacture defects deliberately or model normality instead, and both have consequences the buyer discovers late.
advance_criteria: Anomaly-detection approaches deployed on good-part data alone at production yield
Defect libraries shared across plants or vendors

task/industrial-welding.short_description: Joining metal parts by arc or spot welding to a specified procedure, repeatably and to a standard someone will inspect.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Automotive body shops have welded robotically at enormous scale for decades; the process physics, the equipment and the qualification path are all settled. What is unsettled is who else can afford it — the job shop with a welder shortage and a hundred part numbers — and that is a setup-cost problem, not a maturity one. Cobot welding is the interesting frontier, and it is tracked separately as an approach.
advance_criteria: Already at the top of the scale for repeat-volume parts
regress_criteria: A joining-method shift, such as structural adhesives displacing welds in volume assemblies

evidence_considered.sentence: Robotic arc welding cell maturity MATURE

incumbent_process.text: A certified welder working from a drawing and a weld procedure, with quality riding on that individual's hand and day.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Manual welding is skilled, hot, and increasingly hard to staff; the shortage of certified welders is the reason this task keeps returning to the automation agenda.
advance_criteria: Stable.

approaches.short_description: A collaborative arm with a torch, taught by hand-guiding, aimed at the job shop that welds fifty of something rather than fifty thousand.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: This is the sharpest product-market fit in the cobot category: welder shortages are acute, the units are cheap enough to buy without a capital committee, and hand-guided teaching means the existing welder programs it. It is not mature because weld quality sign-off and duty cycle still send the hard work back to the fenced cell.
advance_criteria: Certified weld procedures accepted on cobot-welded parts as routine
Job shops reporting a second and third unit after the first
Teaching times that beat an experienced welder's setup on a small batch
regress_criteria: Quality rejections in regulated work pushing shops back to manual welding

approaches.short_description: A fenced arm with a welding torch and positioner, programmed offline for a fixed part family.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Automotive has welded robotically for decades and the process is thoroughly characterised. What keeps the rest of the market manual is not welding physics but fixturing and programming cost, which scales with part variety, not with the number of robots.
advance_criteria: Already at the top of the scale for repeat-volume parts
regress_criteria: A shift to joining methods that robots handle less well than humans

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Parts do not arrive where the program thinks they are. Touch sensing, laser seam tracking or through-arc tracking is what separates a cell that welds parts from a cell that welds air.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by upstream tolerances tight enough to weld blind, which job-shop economics rule out.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Torch cleaning, wire feed and tip changes are the unglamorous reasons a welding cell stops; unattended running depends on them more than on the motion program.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by automatic torch servicing running a full shift unattended.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: In structural, pressure or transport work the weld must satisfy a code and an inspector. A robot that lays a good-looking bead but cannot be qualified is unsellable into exactly the segments that pay best.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by codes and inspectors treating robotic procedures as routine.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Large weldments in agriculture, construction and rail equipment run in medium volume with code-qualified procedures, which suits a fenced cell.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Body-in-white spot welding is the largest installed base of welding robots in the world.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: This is where the welder shortage is most acute and where the cobot welding cell finds its buyer.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Where the weld is inspected against a code, the customer's quality department, not the plant manager, decides whether the robot runs. That approval cycle is slow and is rarely counted in the payback model.
advance_criteria: Robotic weld procedures accepted as routine by third-party inspectors
In-process weld monitoring accepted in place of destructive sampling

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: A shop with two hundred part numbers cannot pay for two hundred programs. Offline programming and hand-guided teaching exist, but the honest measure is whether a welder can teach a new part before lunch, and usually they cannot.
advance_criteria: Teaching a new weldment in under an hour by shop staff
CAD-driven program generation used in production, not demonstrations

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: The weld fixture holds tolerance the robot cannot recover. It is engineered per part family and frequently costs more than the robot, which is why welding automation stalls in high-mix shops.
advance_criteria: Modular fixturing reconfigured by shop staff for a new part family
Sensing good enough to weld parts held in generic clamping

task/lightning-protection-testing.short_description: Verifying continuity of the blade lightning protection system between receptors and the tower ground path.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Aerones sells robotic LPS continuity testing commercially and it is a natural add-on for any suspended platform already on the blade. Volume is limited by how often owners test, which is annual at most, so it will follow cleaning rather than lead it.
advance_criteria: LPS testing bundled into standard inspection campaigns
More than one vendor selling it
Certification bodies accepting robot-generated test records

incumbent_process.text: Technician continuity measurement from rope access or platform.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: The test itself is simple; the cost is entirely access.
advance_criteria: Stable.

approaches.short_description: A robot lowered from the nacelle on ropes or cables and positioned against the blade for cleaning, coating, testing and repair.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Aerones and Rope Robotics sell suspended-robot cleaning, leading-edge protection and lightning-protection testing commercially to multiple owners; structural repair from the same platforms is still in pilot. Early commercial for the approach overall, with the caveat that repair specifically is a step behind.
advance_criteria: Structural repair sold as a standard service, not a trial
Fleets operating in more than one continent per vendor
Multi-year service agreements that name robotic maintenance

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Owners carry the insurance obligation to test.
advance_criteria: Stable.

market/machine-tending.short_description: The robot-adjacent work around a machine or a line — loading and unloading machines, stacking output, joining, checking and assembling parts. The oldest robotics market and still the one that buys the most arms.

market/manufacturing.short_description: Discrete and process manufacturing: assembly, machine tending, welding, painting, material handling on the factory floor.

market/material-movement.short_description: Moving pallets, cases, totes and each-items inside distribution centres and fulfilment sites; the domain where autonomous mobile robots reached scale first.

market/oil-and-gas.short_description: Upstream, midstream, and downstream hydrocarbon assets requiring hazardous inspection and maintenance.

architecture_note.text: Tendon-driven, deliberately compliant actuation instead of rigid geared joints, which lowers the injury risk in a home but caps peak force and complicates precise position control.

task/pallet-movement.short_description: Moving full pallets between dock, storage, staging and production areas without a human forklift operator.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Autonomous pallet jacks and forklifts are in repeated paid deployments across 3PLs and manufacturers, sold by at least five vendors with multi-site customers and a Rockwell-owned incumbent. Brownfield variability, dock edge cases and safety certification still limit penetration to a small share of forklift hours, which is why this is scaling rather than mature.
advance_criteria: Autonomous units exceeding a double-digit share of new pallet-truck purchases at large 3PLs
Standardised safety certification accepted across regions
Routine trailer loading and unloading without human intervention
Fleet-level WMS integration sold as a product, not a project
regress_criteria: Vendor consolidation that removes multi-vendor competition
A safety incident that triggers regulatory restriction

evidence_considered.sentence: Vecna Robotics targets task Pallet movement
OTTO Motors targets task Pallet movement
Fox Robotics targets task Pallet movement
Third Wave Automation targets task Pallet movement
AMR pallet jack or lift maturity SCALING

incumbent_process.text: Manual forklift operators, typically on multiple shifts with high turnover.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Forklift operation is one of the largest hourly labour categories in logistics and the labour-model change is the whole business case.
advance_criteria: Stable.

approaches.short_description: Retrofit kits or purpose-built forklifts that drive, lift and enter trailers autonomously.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Fox Robotics and Third Wave Automation sell autonomous forklifts into paying customer sites, with trailer work as the wedge, but customer counts are small and the trailer edge cases are still being worked through site by site. A step behind the pallet-jack approach on repeatability.
advance_criteria: Repeat multi-site orders from the same customers
Unattended trailer unloading across the full inbound mix
A major forklift OEM shipping autonomy as a factory option

approaches.short_description: Fixed automated storage and retrieval systems that move pallets or cases within a structure instead of with vehicles.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Fixed AS/RS is a decades-old category with standard integrators and financing; Symbotic-style systems extend it to case handling at grocery scale. There is no technology question left, only capital allocation.
advance_criteria: Already mature

approaches.short_description: Purpose-built autonomous pallet trucks and lift trucks that move pallets at floor level or to low rack positions.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Seegrid, Vecna and OTTO Motors sell autonomous pallet trucks into repeat multi-site deployments with 3PLs and manufacturers, and the category has a Rockwell-owned incumbent. It is scaling rather than mature because penetration is still a small fraction of pallet-truck hours and each site remains a project.
advance_criteria: Autonomous units as a standard line item in 3PL fleet purchases
Order-to-first-shift under a month at brownfield sites
Mixed-vendor fleets orchestrated by a customer-owned system

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Pallet trucks share aisles with pedestrians and manual forklifts; certified safety fields and speed limits determine throughput.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed in fully segregated automated zones.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Fork entry into damaged, wrapped or misaligned pallets is the highest-frequency failure mode; 3D perception of the pockets is the core capability.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by standardised pallet quality, which no DC has.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Dock plates, trailer floors, lighting changes and tight clearances break navigation assumptions; this is where pilots stall.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by automated dock equipment.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Missions originate in the WMS; without integration the robot is a remote-controlled truck.
advance_criteria: Would be simplified by standard WMS robot interfaces such as VDA 5050 becoming universal.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Line-side to warehouse pallet flows in CPG plants are repetitive and 24/7.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Retail distribution centres are the largest pallet-flow sites.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: 3PLs run many similar sites and buy in fleets once one site proves out.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Removing operators changes shift structures, union agreements and supervisor roles. Sites that only reassign drivers to exception handling do not realise the savings that justified the purchase.
advance_criteria: Customers reporting realised labour savings, not projected ones
Repeat purchases by the same customer across sites

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Pallet quality, stacking patterns and staging rules differ by shift and by customer, and the robot inherits every exception the humans quietly handled. The fix is process discipline, which the vendor cannot sell.
advance_criteria: Exception rates published and trending below human error rates
Robots handling damaged or non-standard pallets without escalation

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Certification to regional standards for driverless industrial trucks is slow and site-specific, and it caps travel speed, which caps throughput. Customers with global footprints want one certificate, not one per region.
advance_criteria: Harmonised standards accepted across the US and EU
Certified higher-speed operation in mixed traffic
Insurers treating certified fleets as standard risk

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Most sites were laid out for human drivers; racking, aisle widths and floor quality vary, and every pilot becomes a site-engineering project. Vendors win when they can deploy without changing the building.
advance_criteria: Deployments quoted from a site survey without custom engineering
Vendors publishing site-readiness criteria that customers can self-assess
Sub-month time from order to first autonomous shift

task/palletizing.short_description: Stacking cases, bags or trays onto a pallet at the end of a production line, to a pattern and at line rate.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: A box on a conveyor is the friendliest object in manufacturing: known geometry, known pose, known rate. Vendors quote guaranteed case rates, dozens of integrators compete, and cobot palletizers have pushed the price down to where a single line can justify one. Nothing here is a research question; the argument is footprint and price.
advance_criteria: Already at the top of the scale; mixed-SKU pattern building is the remaining frontier
regress_criteria: A shift to packaging formats that defeat vacuum and clamp tooling

incumbent_process.text: Operators lifting cases off a conveyor onto a pallet by hand, or a fixed mechanical layer palletizer built for one pattern.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Manual palletizing is among the highest injury-rate jobs in a plant, and the mechanical alternative cannot change pattern without retooling — which is why the robot displaced both.
advance_criteria: Stable.

approaches.short_description: A collaborative arm on a wheeled base or lift column, moved between lines and set up by an operator rather than an integrator.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Packaged cobot palletizers are sold by every cobot vendor and several specialists, and small manufacturers buy them precisely because there is no integration project. They stay a step behind the fixed cell because payload and reach cap the case rate, so they win the low-volume line and lose the high one. Scaling rather than mature until they take share on the fast lines too.
advance_criteria: Cobot palletizers quoted at case rates competitive with fixed cells
Operators reconfiguring patterns without vendor support as the norm
Repeat purchases across multiple lines at the same plant
regress_criteria: Payload and speed limits proving a hard ceiling, confining these to demonstration lines

approaches.short_description: A dedicated arm at the end of a line stacking cases or bags to a pattern, usually with a vacuum or clamp tool.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: End-of-line palletizing is the single most standardised robot application in existence: the part geometry is a box, the pattern is software, and the vendors sell it as a configured product with a quoted rate. Buyers argue about price and footprint, not feasibility.
advance_criteria: Already at the top of the scale; watch mixed-SKU pattern building as the next frontier
regress_criteria: None credible

technical_requirements.text: Tooling that holds the actual package

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Vacuum works on a sealed case and fails on a shrink-wrapped bundle or a bag; the end effector, not the arm, decides whether a given plant's product can be palletized at all.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by tooling that spans case, bag and tray without a change.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Single-SKU patterns are solved. Building a stable mixed pallet from an arbitrary order is a packing problem plus a stability problem, and it is where the remaining engineering sits.
advance_criteria: Would be satisfied by mixed-case pallets built at rate without human correction.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: High case volumes, hard washdown environments and severe manual-handling injury exposure make this the densest palletizing buyer.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Consumer goods lines run continuously with stable case formats, which is the best possible fit for a fixed palletizing cell.
advance_criteria: Stable.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Marketing changes the pack format and the tooling stops working. The cell's lifetime is tied to a package design decision that the plant does not control.
advance_criteria: Tooling changes handled in-house within a shift
Cells requalified for a new pack format without vendor engineering

blockers.text: Floor space at the end of the line

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Plants were laid out before the cell existed, and the end of the line is the most congested place in the building. This is the single most common reason a justified palletizer does not get installed.
advance_criteria: Cells with a footprint small enough to drop in without moving the line
Vendors quoting installation without a plant layout change

economics_notes.text: Payback is usually argued on injury and turnover as much as on headcount, because manual case stacking carries some of the highest recordable injury rates in a plant.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Plants that only count hourly wages undervalue the cell; the insurance and absence line is often the larger number, though it varies enough by employer that it should not be quoted as a rule.
advance_criteria: Would firm up with published customer injury-rate data before and after installation.

architecture_note.text: The hands are the product thesis: high-DOF hydraulic hands aimed at human-equivalent manipulation, on the bet that dexterity, not locomotion, is what gates useful work.

architecture_note.text: The arm ships with an integrated camera in the wrist rather than a third-party vision kit, which is the whole positioning: the customer buys one supported product instead of integrating two.

task/tower-nacelle-inspection.short_description: External inspection of towers, nacelle housings and transition pieces for corrosion, coating failure and bolt issues.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: The same drone fleets that inspect blades increasingly cover towers and nacelles in the same visit, and offshore operators buy it to defer technician transfers. It is not yet universal practice because tower inspection is lower value per finding than blade inspection.
advance_criteria: Tower and nacelle coverage bundled by default in fleet inspection contracts
Standardised defect taxonomies accepted by certification bodies
Routine offshore use without vessel support

incumbent_process.text: Rope-access or platform inspection by technicians during scheduled maintenance.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Structural inspections were historically bundled into technician maintenance visits.
advance_criteria: Stable.

approaches.short_description: Multirotor drones flying close to blades for inspection; contact work from the same platform is early.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: For inspection the drone approach is mature and fleet-wide; for contact work such as cleaning or coating it is early. Rated as scaling for the approach as a whole because the inspection business funds the contact experiments and the same vendors sell both.
advance_criteria: Contact tasks (cleaning, coating) sold commercially from a drone platform
Autonomous, operator-free inspection flights as the default
BVLOS approvals for fleet campaigns in major markets

assessment.author: editorial

advance_criteria: Stable.

task/truck-unloading.short_description: Unloading pallets or floor-loaded cases from trailers at the receiving dock without a human operator.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Robotic trailer unloading runs at early customer sites for both palletised (autonomous forklift) and floor-loaded (arm-based) freight, but it is not routine: trailer condition, lighting and load variability make every trailer an edge case. Vendors report throughput on good trailers, not on the fleet average.
advance_criteria: Unattended operation across a customer's full inbound trailer mix
Throughput parity with a human crew on the fleet average
Repeat orders from more than one customer

incumbent_process.text: Manual forklift drivers for palletised freight; manual crews for floor-loaded cases.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Unloading is one of the hardest jobs to staff at a DC, which is the pull.
advance_criteria: Stable.

approaches.short_description: Retrofit kits or purpose-built forklifts that drive, lift and enter trailers autonomously.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Fox Robotics and Third Wave Automation sell autonomous forklifts into paying customer sites, with trailer work as the wedge, but customer counts are small and the trailer edge cases are still being worked through site by site. advance_criteria: Repeat multi-site orders from the same customers
Unattended trailer unloading across the full inbound mix
A major forklift OEM shipping autonomy as a factory option
